testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air, what does this mean?

options.text: This is normal and you should not worry.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if the system pressure gets too high. If it is releasing air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic repair the brakes.

questions.question: What must be on an air tank in a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have a one-way check valve between the air compressor and the first tank. This stops air from flowing back out if there is a leak.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If these liquids build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, what should you never do?
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The force from both the springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Which vehicles must have emergency brakes?

options.text: They are not required on trucks.
They are only required on trailers.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must work by mechanical force.

questions.question: What happens if brakes become too hot?

options.text: The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: If brakes overheat from heavy use, they may stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: What helps prevent the wheels from locking up when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up while the brakes are being used.

questions.question: What color are ABS warning lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems have yellow warning lamps.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving?

options.text: Stop and park where you are.
Leave the roadway and park safely as soon as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the roadway and park safely as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving, safely exit the roadway and park as soon as you can. If air pressure drops too low, your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: Brakes may get out of adjustment if:
questions.explanation: Brakes can go out of adjustment quickly when they overheat from use. Check your brake adjustment often.

questions.question: Emergency brakes must use what type of force?
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. So emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force to hold the brakes on.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, the best way to use your brakes is to:

options.text: Keep using the brakes the whole way down.
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this as you go down the hill.
Use the brakes only near the bottom of the hill.
Press the brake pedal steadily the whole way down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this as you go down the hill.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use the engine to help slow your vehicle. Apply the brakes just enough to feel the vehicle slow down. Then release them when you are about 5 mph below your safe speed. Repeat this process as you go down the hill.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty trucks use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty trucks have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most new heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most new heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brakes that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold air for only one braking use.
Hold enough air for several braking uses if the compressor stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several braking uses if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air so the brakes can still work several times if the compressor fails.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997, and other vehicles with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but each has separate hoses and lines.
Both systems use the same hoses and lines.
One is the main system and one is a backup if the first one fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in very wet weather with freezing temperatures?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release on their own.
The brakes may become too slippery to work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in very wet weather when it is below freezing. The brakes could freeze in place and prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: When you need to make an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Turn your trailer to the right and stop.
Turn your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. You should still be able to turn if needed.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work better.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if air pressure is low. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: Brake fade happens because of:
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment when:

options.text: One side is used more than the other side.

questions.explanation: Hot brakes are more likely to get out of adjustment. Use proper braking methods to avoid overheating your brakes.

questions.question: The ____ shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with air brakes has a supply pressure gauge. It shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.
